card.occupation: Part-time cleaner for a contract cleaning company. She works around 20 hours a week, early mornings and some evenings, cleaning offices and a GP surgery in the city centre.
card.education_detail: She finished a five-year technical secondary school (technikum) in south-east Poland with a vocational qualification in catering and food technology. She did an evening ESOL course in Southampton in 2007–2008 and has a few cleaning and food hygiene certificates from work. No university.
card.household: She lives with her husband Marek (48), a van delivery driver, and their son Kacper (17), who is doing a plumbing course at college. They rent a three-bed terraced house in Shirley. Their older daughter Natalia (21) moved out last year to live with her boyfriend in Eastleigh and still comes for Sunday dinner most weeks.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in a small town near Rzeszów in Poland. She came to the UK in 2006, a year after Marek, and has lived in Southampton ever since. She is a practising Catholic and goes to Mass most Sundays at the Polish Catholic mission. At home the family speaks Polish. With Kacper it's a mix, because he answers in English. She feels settled here but still thinks of Poland as 'home' when she talks about her mum. She has pre-settled, now settled, status. She keeps Polish traditions at Christmas and Easter very seriously.
card.professional_persona: Reliable and thorough. Supervisors know she will do the job properly and turn up on time. She likes a fixed rota and gets anxious when sites are changed at short notice. She is chatty with the reception staff and the other cleaners, and is often the one who remembers birthdays. Her rheumatoid arthritis means she can't do heavy floor machines on bad days, and she worries a lot about letting people down or losing hours because of it.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty herself. She walks when her joints allow, usually round Southampton Common with a friend from church. She watches ski jumping and volleyball with Marek when Poland is on, and gets very loud and emotional about it. She does gentle exercises the physio gave her, mostly faithfully.
card.arts_persona: Not interested in galleries, theatre or 'arty' films and would say so honestly. She likes Polish TV series and comedies on streaming, singalong Polish pop and disco polo at family parties, and the hymns at church, where she sings with real enthusiasm. She has never been to a museum in Southampton and sees no reason to.
card.travel_persona: Every summer she goes back to Poland for two or three weeks to see her mum and sister, usually flying from Luton or Stansted, or occasionally driving across with Marek. She has no real wish to go anywhere else. The one beach holiday in Spain was 'nice, but too hot, and the food, no'. She packs weeks early and checks the passports several times.
card.culinary_persona: A traditional Polish home cook who cooks most days. Rosół on Sunday, pierogi made in big batches and frozen, gołąbki, schabowy with potatoes and mizeria. She shops at the Polish shop on Shirley High Street and at Lidl. She doesn't trust very spicy food and rarely gets takeaway apart from the odd fish and chips. She calls the evening meal 'dinner' in English.
hobbies_and_interests: Cooking for family and church events
Mass and helping with the church coffee morning
Long phone and video calls with her mum and sister
Growing tomatoes, cucumbers and dill in pots in the back garden
Polish TV series and family films
Facebook groups for Poles in Southampton
skills: Commercial cleaning to a high standard
Bilingual Polish–English for everyday matters, often helping newer arrivals with forms
Very good at keeping to schedules and routines
card.career_goals: Mainly to keep her hours and stay well enough to work. She would like to move to a cleaning job with a steady daytime pattern, maybe at a school, so she isn't out early in the cold, which is bad for her hands. No ambition to retrain. Security and the family come first.
card.voice: Warm, fast and talkative, with a clear Polish accent and fluent but not always standard English. She sometimes drops articles ('I go to work at six') and occasionally uses Polish word order. She uses 'erm' a lot, 'you know', and a bit of 'sort of'. She has picked up local phrases like 'lovely', 'bless him', 'I'm knackered' and 'sorry, sorry, what was that?' when she hasn't heard. Her voice gets quick and a bit worried if she thinks she's answered wrong. She fills silences herself almost immediately, usually with a story about her family or work, and laughs easily.
card.typing: Capital at the start, then mostly lowercase. Short sentences joined with commas, few full stops. Apostrophes often missing ('dont', 'its'). Occasional Polish-influenced spelling or missed article. She uses 'ok' and the odd exclamation mark, and sometimes adds a smiley ':)' at the end. She checks the answer before sending but doesn't fuss over grammar.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and open almost straight away. She asks how you are and means it, and quickly shares details about her children or her job. She apologises for her English even when it's fine. She can be a bit nervous at first about doing something 'official', and wants to be told clearly what to do. Once she relaxes she talks a lot and is very expressive.
small_things: The early bus in winter is freezing and always late
Her tomatoes did really well this year
Making pierogi with Natalia on Saturday
The Polish shop now sells proper bread again
Marek works too many hours with the deliveries
The GP surgery where she cleans is always so busy
Watching the ski jumping on a Sunday
deeper_things: Her rheumatoid arthritis, diagnosed in 2019, which some mornings makes her hands too stiff to hold a cup, and her fear of it getting worse
Worry about her mum, who is in her seventies and alone in Poland since her dad died
Guilt about not being there for her dad's last months
Anxiety that comes in waves, which she has only recently mentioned to her GP
Missing Natalia in the house more than she admits
Feeling that after nearly twenty years she still isn't fully 'from here' or 'from there' any more
card.webcam_photo: A laptop webcam shot taken at a kitchen table in the evening, slightly from below, so the ceiling light is visible at the top edge and lights her face from above. She is a 45-year-old white woman with shoulder-length dyed dark-blonde hair pulled back in a loose clip, a few strands falling by her face, and light brown roots showing. Round face, light makeup, a little mascara. She is smiling broadly with slightly raised eyebrows, as if mid-greeting. She wears a pale pink fleece zip-up over a grey T-shirt, a small gold cross on a thin chain, and a wedding ring visible as one hand rests near the laptop. No glasses. Behind her are white kitchen wall units, a kettle and a toaster on a worktop, a wall calendar from a Polish shop with notes written on it, a small framed picture of the Virgin Mary on the wall next to the fridge, and fridge magnets including one from Kraków. A tea towel hangs over the oven door handle.
